So the target molecule is a combination? Actually that list seems to be two SMILES: a complex heterocycle and a sulfonyl chloride aromatic. Probably the target molecule is a product of a reaction between those two? The template is nitro reduction. The mapped_rxn shows a nitro group being reduced to NH2. The template likely transforms a nitro aromatic to an aniline. The target molecule likely contains an aniline (NH2) group. Indeed the mapped_rxn product side includes [NH2:15] attached to aromatic. So the target product is the molecule with NH2. The precursors would be the nitro version (with NO2) and maybe other reagents? The template likely is a transformation of nitro to amine, so the precursor is the nitro compound (same rest of molecule) and maybe a reducing agent (like H2, Fe/HCl). But the template likely only defines the transformation of the substrate; the other reagent may be omitted. In apply_template tool, we need to apply template to target molecule to get precursors. Let's use apply_template with molecule_smiles being the target product (the complex heterocycle? Actually the product is the first SMILES? Wait the first SMILES is "CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc(N)cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1". That contains an N attached to aromatic with N (maybe an aniline). Indeed c2cc(N)cc3... So that is the product with NH2. The second SMILES is a sulfonyl chloride, maybe a protecting group? Not relevant to nitro reduction. The template likely applies to the first SMILES only. So we need to apply template 2895 to that SMILES to get nitro precursor. Let's call apply_template.
